Welcome to Aincrad RPG! This section will guide you through everything you need to know as a new player.
Download the latest Aincrad launcher to get started:
Download and install the Aincrad launcher
Create your first character (choose your vocation: Wizard, Archer, or Duelist)
Explore the first level and complete tutorial quests
Reach level 20 to receive your vocation-specific starter kit and directions to the first Warden
Focus on completing the tutorial quests in the starting area. These will give you essential equipment and teach you the game basics.

Upon reaching level 20, you'll receive a vocation-specific starter kit (including item upgrades and a promotion) and directions to the first Warden. Proceed with caution- Wardens are powerful enemies that require preparation and often a party to defeat. Make sure you're well-equipped and ready before attempting the boss.

Aincrad is a progression MMO set within the tower—a mysterious vertical labyrinth of ever-changing levels. Players form guilds of Pathfinders, regroup and trade in Plazas, and challenge each Level's Warden to unlock the next rise.

The game is set in an endless, seasonal, shifting labyrinth of levels inside the tower. The labyrinth reconfigures over time as routes and configurations rewrite themselves, making exploration and progression a dynamic experience.

Every season begins with the Shift—a seasonal update that introduces new Levels, Wardens, mechanics, and content. The labyrinth reconfigures, routes rewrite themselves, and Pathfinders race to push higher through the new challenges.
Players form guilds of Pathfinders—elite adventurers who push forward to unlock new Levels and face the most dangerous content.
Wardens- Each Level has a powerful boss that must be defeated to unlock the next rise
Plazas- Safe zones where players regroup, trade, and prepare for their next challenge
Progression- Advance through Levels by defeating Wardens and completing challenges
Form guilds with other players. Teamwork makes progressing through Levels much easier and more efficient.
Aincrad has three base vocations, each with two ascendancy classes(promotions) that unlock at level 20. Your vocation defines your combat role, stat growth, and playstyle.
Each vocation has unique strengths, weaknesses, and specializations. Your choice determines:
Combat style- Melee, ranged, or magic
Spell arsenal- Unique spells and abilities
Stat progression- How your character's attributes grow
Equipment preferences- Optimal gear for your playstyle
High HP, dual wield, aggressive combat
High mana, magic shield, powerful spells
Each base vocation has two ascendancy paths to choose from. Ascendancy is unlocked as you progress:

Choose your vocation carefully when creating your character. Each base vocation offers a unique gameplay experience — Wizards excel at high-damage spellcasting, Archers are versatile ranged fighters, and Duelists dominate close-quarters combat with dual-wielding.
Magic user with the highest mana growth and a built-in magic shield. Promotes into Elementalist(elemental penetration, element swapping) or Priest(group heals, buffs, holy magic).
Ranged specialist with balanced HP and mana. Promotes into Zenbow(elemental arrow buffs, Zen Focus double-attack passive) or Sharpshooter(increased damage per tile distance from the target).

Aggressive melee fighter with the highest HP growth and native dual wield. Promotes into Berserker(rage, more damage and attack speed as HP drops, life leech) or Warden(shield-scaling damage, Bulwark stacks).
You choose your vocation when creating your character. This is a permanent choice for that character, so consider:
Playstyle preference— Do you prefer melee, ranged, or magic?
Role preference— Do you want to burst down enemies, sustain through fights, or support?
Group composition— What does your team need?
The first Warden is a powerful enemy. Make sure you're well-equipped and consider forming a party before attempting to fight it.
You can create multiple characters with different vocations to experience all playstyles. Each character progresses independently.
Magic user with the highest mana growth and a built-in magic shield. Wizards deal through spells and area magic.

The Elementalist commands multiple elements and can swap between them depending on the situation. Their attacks benefit from elemental penetration, allowing them to cut through enemy resistances more effectively than other magic classes.
The Priest supports and heals the group through dedicated healing spells and buffs, while also wielding holy magic to defend against enemies in combat.
Ranged specialist with balanced HP and mana growth. Archers deal physical and distance damage from range.
The Zenbow is a mystical archer who empowers auto-attacks with elemental arrow buffs.
Passive — Zen Focus: 20% chance to immediately fire a second attack after the first. The second hit also triggers the active arrow buff's effects.
The Sharpshooter is a long-range precision fighter who gains increased damage based on distance— the further away the target, the harder the hit.
Aggressive melee fighter with the highest HP growth and native dual wield— equip a weapon in each hand.

The Berserker thrives on the edge of death. As their HP drops, they deal more damage and attack faster— making low health a weapon. Berserkers also have passive life leech, sustaining themselves through combat by draining life with every strike.
The Warden is a defensive fighter who deals bonus damage that scales with their shield's defense value. They build Bulwark stacks by blocking attacks, unlocking progressively stronger bonuses.
+10% block chance, reflect 10% of damage taken
+15% block chance, reflect 20% of damage taken
Reflected damage gains a flat bonus equal to (shield defense × 0.5). Stacks expire after 15 seconds without a block.

Item crafting Uber Monsters Reward Orbs
Reward orbs are special drops that appear when skulled monsters (uber monsters) die, containing gold and crafting currency.

When a skulled monster dies, it has a 100% chance to drop reward orbs. These orbs spawn near the monster's death location and must be collected by standing on them (or auto-looted if enabled). Each orb contains money and crafting currency used in the Item Crafting system.
Orbs spawn over 10 seconds with visual effects
Players must stand on the orb to collect it (unless auto-loot is enabled)
All players who damaged the monster are eligible to receive orbs
Red and Black skull monsters have a 20% chance to drop 2 orbs instead of 1

Reward orbs drop money and crafting currency. The amount of money and type of crafting currency varies based on the monster's skull tier and base HP. Higher tier monsters drop more valuable rewards. Crafting currency is used to modify and improve equipment in the Item Crafting system.
Enhanced versions of existing monsters that spawn randomly with unique modifiers and increased difficulty.

Uber monsters are rare, powerful variants of regular monsters that have a 5% chance to respawn as uber when a normal monster dies. They feature special abilities, stat modifications, and unique combat mechanics that make them significantly more challenging than their normal counterparts.
Every uber monster receives one modifier that significantly changes their behavior and combat mechanics.
Uber monsters come in four tiers, each with increasing difficulty and rewards:
When a monster respawns as uber, the tier distribution is:
Applies random debuffs to enemies (50% chance every 6s)
Attacks with death magic, cursing enemies and reducing healing
Attacks with holy light, reducing enemy accuracy
Burns enemies with fire attacks and applies fire damage over time
Deals up to 50% more damage as health decreases
Drains life from enemies, healing itself (80% chance every 4s)
Drains mana from enemies (80% chance every 4s)
Explodes on death, dealing massive area damage (3x3 area, 3s warning)
Freezes enemies with ice attacks, slowing movement
Gains resistance to the last damage type it took (+30% resistance)
Has a chance to put enemies to sleep (40% chance every 6s)
Has a chance to stun enemies on attack (30% chance every 5s)
Periodically deals damage in an area around itself (every 4s)
Periodically gains a damage-absorbing shield (every 15s, 5s duration)
Periodically phases out, becoming harder to target (every 10s)
Periodically summons minions to aid it (60% chance every 10s, max 3)
Poisons enemies with toxic attacks that deal damage over time
Pulls nearby players adjacent to itself (70% chance every 6s)
Pushes players away from itself (60% chance every 5s)
Reflects 25% of damage back to attackers (30% chance)
Summons rotating orbs around targeted players (every 3s, 8s duration)
Summons undead minions when damaged (3 skeletons, 2s cooldown)
Takes 50% reduced damage from all sources
Teleports near its target periodically (60% chance every 8s)

Uber monsters are significantly more powerful than their normal counterparts, with higher tiers being exponentially more dangerous. Always be prepared for their unique modifiers and plan your approach accordingly. Higher tier ubers (Red and Black skull) require careful coordination and preparation.

This server adds a Path-of-Exile–style item layer on top of normal Tibia items.
Every eligible equipment item can have:
Quality(0–20): scales the item's base stats
Rarity(Normal → Legendary): determined by the number of modifiers on the item
Modifiers: extra stats that change how your attacks and spells behave
This guide explains what these mean, how they work, and how crafting currencies interact with them.
Not every item can roll these properties.
Ammo (excluded from quality scaling and usually excluded from properties)
If an item is not eligible, it simply won't gain these properties.
Quality increases an item's base stats by a percentage.
It does not change the item's modifiers. Quality only scales what the item already "is" underneath.
Depending on the item type, Quality can scale:
Weapon Attack(physical and the native elemental portion)
Quality scaling always moves values in the "stronger" direction:
Positive values increase using half-up rounding
Negative values move toward 0(less negative), never further away
Rarity is determined by the number of modifiers on an item.
When you add or remove modifiers, the item's rarity automatically updates to match the new modifier count.
Modifiers are extra properties on top of the base item. They come in two types:
Add a fixed amount to stats.
Percent modifiers scale a base that includes the item's native/base contribution(not only "other modifiers").

This table shows a sample of available modifiers. The full system includes modifiers for all seven elements (energy, fire, ice, earth, holy, death, physical) across multiple categories. Modifier values scale with item tier/level.
Modifiers can apply differently depending on whether the damage comes from an Attack or a Spell.
An Attack is a weapon-driven hit:
Wand hits (their on-hit element is still an "attack source")
A Spell is something you cast:
Rune-like spell effects (if treated as spells)
A hit can have multiple elemental components (physical, fire, ice, energy, etc.).
If a modifier adds an element, and the hit does not already have that element component:
The element component is created, as long as the modifier matches the hit's source type(attack vs spell).
+10 fire attack damage on a pure physical sword hit:
Creates a fire component and adds +10 fire to it
A wand that normally deals energy(attack source)
The hit keeps its energy component
And gains a new fire component (+10)
+10% fire damage applies to fire damage from attacks and spells.
Applies only to attack hits(weapon-based hits)
Adds +10 to the hit's fire component
If the hit has no fire component, it creates one
Example: Wand of Vortex (base energy hit) Result: energy base+ new fire component
Applies only to spell hits(casted spells)
Adds +10 to the spell's fire component
If the spell has no fire component, it creates one
Example: exori hur that normally deals physical Result: physical base+ new fire component
Applies to all fire damage, regardless of source:
Scales the total fire base (native + flat adds)
These currencies mutate rarity, modifiers, and quality(when allowed by item eligibility).
You can only change Quality/Rarity/Modifiers while the item is NOT equipped.

Aincrad is a custom Tibia server based on protocol 13.21, featuring unique RPG elements like Aincrad vocations and advanced progression systems beyond traditional leveling.
Yes, Aincrad is completely free to download and play. The server is open to everyone and can be played online via our offical client.

l: How do I download and install Aincrad?
p: Download the Aincrad launcher from the download page. The launcher will handle the installation and setup for you.

l: How do I choose my vocation?
p: You choose your vocation when creating your character. This choice is permanent for that character, so choose based on your preferred playstyle.
Visit the Vocations Guide to learn about all available vocations and find the one that fits your playstyle.

l: What client version does Aincrad use?
p: Aincrad uses a custom client based on OTClient using protocol 13.21.
Aincrad uses a custom server based on Canary using protocol 13.21. The server is hosted in Frankfurt, Germany.

l: I'm experiencing lag/crashes. How can I fix this?
p: Try restarting your client, checking your internet connection, or contacting support on Discord for assistance with technical issues. The server is hosted in Frankfurt, Germany, so players closer to that region may experience better latency.

l: Can I play Aincrad on my Mac/Linux computer?
p: Mac and Linux support is currently in development. When available, it will be listed on our download page. Join our Discord to follow development updates.
